Anya (acct): Hey team, we rotated our IdP signing cert last night and now several users get a SAML login failure: 'Invalid signature' right after POST to our ACS. Not seeing obvious logs on our end. :(
Devon (support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the raw SAMLResponse or the SP logs around the post? quick question: did the IdP switch from RSA->ECDSA during rotation?
Anya (acct): IdP Ops confirms they moved to ECDSA P-256. We have a sample SP log:
```
2026-03-15T20:12:03Z ERROR saml: Assertion signature verification failed: unsupported algorithm: ecdsa-sha256
POST /sso/acs 400 23ms
```
Devon (support): That error usually means the SP metadata/validator doesn't have the new key or the certificate in IdP metadata isn't what the IdP served at runtime. Two quick checks: 1) fetch IdP metadata URL from the SP host and inspect KeyDescriptor ordering; 2) check ACS URL exact match (trailing slash / casing).
Ravi (eng): Also check for HTTP redirects on the metadata URL. If the metadata endpoint returns a 302 HTML page (ALB redirect) the SP may have cached an older cert or failed to parse. Can you run: `curl -I https://idp.example.com/metadata` and paste headers?
IdP Ops (customer): Here's the curl we ran from our infra:
```
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 20:10:01 GMT
Location: https://auth.example-idp.net/metadata/
Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8
```
Devon (support): Aha — that Location has a trailing slash and the SP https client might be following to a different host (auth.example-idp.net) where metadata has the new ECDSA cert, but the original domain appears in the EntityID check. That can cause the SP to keep the old key or treat the metadata as unsigned/invalid.
SAML-bot: metadata-refresh-job failed for tenant:acme-corp — http:302 -> aborting parse (reason: non-200 response) :wrench:
Claire (oncall): Workaround: upload the raw x509 cert to the SP tenant settings to get immediate verification while we fix metadata fetch. Also set metadata fetch to follow redirects (or better: point to the canonical host).
Devon (support): Steps I recommend:
1) From your SP host run `curl -sSL https://idp.example.com/metadata | xmllint --noout -` to ensure a proper XML is returned (the -sSL follows 302/301).
2) If xmllint fails, change metadata URL to the final host `https://auth.example-idp.net/metadata/` in the tenant settings.
3) In the SP admin UI, upload the Base64 X509 cert string from the IdP's KeyDescriptor for the signing key.
4) Clear the SAML metadata cache and trigger a metadata refresh.
Devon (support): Example openssl command to verify the cert fingerprint on the PEM IdP provided: `openssl x509 -in idp_signing.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256` then compare to what the SP shows under tenant->SAML certs.
IdP Ops (customer): We matched fingerprints; the problem was the ALB redirect we added during the deploy. The metadata served at the final host used ECDSA but our initial domain responded 302 and the SP rejected parsing. We updated the ALB to return 200 for `/metadata` canonical host.
Ravi (eng): Good. After you change that, please post the output of `curl -sSL https://idp.example.com/metadata | grep -E "<KeyDescriptor|<EntityDescriptor|<X509Certificate" -n` so we can verify ordering and presence of the signing key.
IdP Ops (customer): Pulled metadata after fix — snippet:
```
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.example.com/">
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <KeyInfo>...ECDSA CERT BASE64...</KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```
Devon (support): Looks good. One final note: SP behavior sometimes is sensitive to EntityID exact match (including trailing slash and case). If your SP tenant is configured with `https://idp.example.com` but metadata uses `https://idp.example.com/` it can fail verification on some libs. Recommend updating tenant entityID to include trailing slash to match metadata.
IdP Ops (customer): Thanks — we changed the tenant entityID to include the slash and restarted the SP service. Users can log in again. :tada:
Claire (oncall): I'll add a KB entry: 'IdP metadata behind redirects + cert rotation -> common signature failure' with the checklist above. Devon — want me to open a follow-up on making our metadata fetch follow redirects and log when non-200 encountered?
Devon (support): Yes please. Make it a P1 doc and attach the curl/xmllint commands and the SAML-bot error if possible. :+1:
SAML-bot: ticket created: SUPPORT-4521 — metadata-fetch-follow-redirects (assigned: eng)
